synthesis.paragraph: In the citation graph, "A co-production approach to identify and visualise vulnerability to urban extreme heat in Nottingham, UK" shares 9 references with the June 15 paper "Analyzing Spatial Variability of the Urban Heat Vulnerability Index in the Face of Climate Change Employing Geospatial Technology in Halifax, Canada", including "Predicting Hospitalization for Heat-Related Illness at the Census-Tract Level", "Mapping Community Determinants of Heat Vulnerability", and "Comparison of impervious surface area and normalized difference vegetation index". The Nottingham paper also shares 7 references with the June 19 paper "Spatial disagreement as decision-support for district-level heat adaptation priorities: Evidence from Taiwan's six major cities", with shared citations including "Mapping Community Determinants of Heat Vulnerability", "The development of a heat wave vulnerability index for London, United Kingdom", and "A Heat Vulnerability Index: Spatial Patterns of Exposure, Sensitivity and Adaptive Capacity for Santiago de Chile". Additionally, "Enhancing senior mobility: the role of public transport attributes in improving travel satisfaction and quality of life" shares 7 references with the July 16 paper "How do non-emergency medical transportation services influence patients’ subjective well-being?", including "Travel and Subjective Well-Being", "Satisfaction with travel and subjective well-being", and "Travel Mode Use, Travel Mode Shift and Subjective Well-Being".
